cells.tense: Right now you are holding two growing things at once and neither one is giving.
cells.act: do the giving in the open this time, where it was always done unseen
cells.ask: Pick a piece of work you've been carrying quietly and do the next part of it where the person it's for can watch. No announcement — just the work, unhidden. Then step back.
cells.core:
You can hold two things that both need you without dropping either. The work gets done, the people around it are looked after, and nothing has to be torn away to free your hands. When what you tended is finished, you step back from it the way a gardener leaves a bed that has taken — no drama, just the next thing.

What's here now is quiet work that nobody sees. You release the finished part alone, in private, so it buys you nothing and asks nothing of you. Do the next part where the person it's for can watch. Not explained, not offered up — just done, in the open. What you set down gets to be visible for once, and you can find out what that does. You already release well; only being seen is missing.
cells.sheetLine: You tend it well. Let it be seen once.
cells.verb: tending what is growing with your own hands until it can stand without you
cells.place: at the moment where you loosen your grip on what you have been carrying

cells.tense: You are already standing past the harvest, planning the next planting.
cells.act: walk through the thing you built and touch nothing
cells.ask: Take a project you finished and walk through it for ten minutes without fixing a single detail. Notice what it already is. Then leave it exactly as it stands.
cells.core:
Your care for what's growing runs ahead of what's here. Two things need tending and you've got a hand on both and an eye on a third that hasn't started, so what's finished is already being planned past. Nothing gets to be done, because done looks like the moment to begin the next one. The grip that keeps things alive is the same grip that won't let one rest.

Being full of a finished thing is what feeds the next growing — not more reaching. Walk through something you already built and touch nothing. Ten minutes, no adjusting, no list of what comes next. Let it be enough as it stands. The satisfaction you're skipping is the fuel; everything else can wait an hour while you stand in what you made.
cells.sheetLine: You're planting again before anything's been harvested.
cells.verb: tending what is growing with your own hands until it can stand without you
cells.place: at the moment where you loosen your grip on what you have been carrying

cells.tense: You were the one who tended it, and you have gone quiet since.
cells.act: carry on with the version you chose through another week of doubt
cells.ask: Return to what you chose to tend and carry the version you picked one more week — no checking whether it's working, no asking anyone. Just the next step.
cells.core:
Things you once tended with your own hands have gone on without you, and the habit of picking them back up is somewhere behind where you're standing now. What's left is watching, and watching doesn't grow anything. The knack for tending is still yours; it's just idling, waiting on a sign that doesn't come.

Hoping is what carries the work when nothing confirms it yet. Return to what you chose and carry it another week — the version you picked, no checking, no asking. Doubt doesn't need answering; it needs outlasting. Take the next step toward it without a sign, and see whether it holds under you. This didn't stop being yours. It has been waiting for you to walk back toward it.
cells.sheetLine: You stopped picking it up. It's still yours to carry.
cells.verb: tending what is growing with your own hands until it can stand without you
cells.place: at the moment where you loosen your grip on what you have been carrying

cells.tense: The work gets done and your name does not land anywhere near it.
cells.act: accept the acknowledgment when it comes
cells.ask: This week, when someone thanks you or names what you did, don't wave it off or hand it to someone else. Let it land and say thank you. Once is enough.
cells.core:
You are keeping something going — quietly, steadily — and if anyone asked you to account for it you'd say you weren't involved. It happens; the one doing it isn't in the picture, including in your own telling. What you set down so something else could grow has stayed unseen, and you've stopped noticing it's missing from the story.

Letting a thank-you land is not the same as asking for credit. When one comes, take it and say thank you instead of passing it on. That's the whole move — no explanation owed, no speech. Watch what happens when you stay where you are and don't deflect. What you gave can be known without a word about it, and you can find out what you do when it is.
cells.sheetLine: The work goes on. The one doing it has gone missing.
cells.verb: tending what is growing with your own hands until it can stand without you
cells.place: at the moment where you loosen your grip on what you have been carrying

attempts.check: The record supports the card's shape but not a person's motive, history, or what anyone near them feels — every cell stays on what the capacity is doing in a moment they could recognise. A reader could reasonably say the tending described is simply being reliable rather than an imbalance, so each core is narrowed to a specific moment (a hand on a finished thing, a plan three steps out) rather than a verdict about their life. The asks survive being wrong: each is one small act that teaches something about tending and release even if the read misses, and none depends on anyone else's response. The sentence that serves me more than them would be any line about 'learning to let go' as a lesson — dropped; the cells say what release is for here, not what the person should feel.
